stories.text: In 1968 a coal-fired power station with eight cooling towers began generating here. It became the last coal-fired power station in Britain, and when it shut in September 2024 it ended 142 years of coal power in the country.

20745.sum: Ratcliffe-on-Soar Power Station is an industrial building.

stories.text: The Wilford Village and Wilford Lane stops, on line 2 from the city centre to Clifton, opened in August 2015.

Coal was found on the Clifton estate, and work on Clifton Colliery began in 1868. Sir Robert Juckes Clifton, the last of the Clifton baronets, died of typhoid in 1869; the colliery and this toll bridge, both his projects, opened in 1870.

For some 400 years a ferry crossed the Trent here, until a temporary wooden footbridge replaced it in 1864. On 16 June 1870 the toll bridge opened, and pedestrians paid a halfpenny to cross; it is still known locally as the Halfpenny Bridge. It was closed to traffic in 1974, and in 1980 its centre span was replaced by a narrower footbridge. In 2014–15 it was widened again to carry the trams of Nottingham Express Transit, and it is now a tram, pedestrian and cycle bridge.

69731.sum: Wilford Toll Bridge, locally referred to as the 'Halfpenny Bridge', is a tram, pedestrian and cycle bridge in Nottingham, England. It crosses the River Trent between the Meadows and Wilford. It originally opened as a toll bridge for general traffic in 1870, but was closed when declared unsafe in 1974.

stories.text: Authorised in 1792 and engineered by William Jessop, the canal opened in 1796 from the Trent to Langley Mill, bringing coal to the town. Railways took its trade; most of the main line was abandoned in 1937.

72555.sum: Canal Museum, on Canal Street. Today it houses Canalhouse. The building was built in 1895, according to OpenStreetMap. It is Grade II listed.

stories.text: E. P. Davis built the Bennerley furnaces, near Ilkeston, in about 1870; by 1880 they belonged to the Awsworth Coal and Iron Company, which was putting up a new furnace.[^grace] A branch of the viaduct's railway served the works. They made their last pig iron in March 1931, and in 1934 Thos. W. Ward of Sheffield bought the three furnaces to take them down.[^grace] The pin is approximate.

In 1876–77 a viaduct was built here of wrought iron, light enough for ground undermined by coal workings. It closed in 1968 but was too costly to take down, and in 2022 it reopened to walkers and cyclists. The only other viaduct like it is Meldon Viaduct in Devon.

147205.sum: Bennerley Viaduct is a former railway bridge, now a foot and cycle bridge, between Ilkeston, Derbyshire, and Awsworth, Nottinghamshire, in central England. It was completed in 1877 and carried the Great Northern Railway's Derbyshire Extension over the River Erewash, which forms the county boundary, and its wide, flat valley. The engineer was Samuel Abbott, who worked under Richard Johnson, the GNR's chief engineer.

stories.text: In 1832 coal owners meeting at the Sun Inn, Eastwood, proposed extending the Mansfield and Pinxton Railway to Leicester. It became the Midland Counties Railway, whose line from Nottingham, at Carrington Street, to Derby opened in 1839.
stories.nm: The railway that began in a pub

150710.sum: Sun Inn is a pub on Derby Road.

aka: Winding House and Headstocks at Bestwood Colliery
178854.cat: Winding House and Headstocks at Bestwood Colliery

stories.text: The Bestwood Coal and Iron Company's colliery here wound up its coal and lowered its miners with a vertical steam engine of 1873. The pit closed in 1967, but the winding engine house and its engine survive.

The Lancaster family sank Bestwood's coal mine in 1875. Beside it the Bestwood Coal and Iron Company opened an ironworks in 1881 with two blast furnaces, added two more in 1890, and kept it working until 1928. The company built the terraces of Park Road, St Albans Road and The Square for its workers, and its offices, with their clock tower, on Park Road.

178854.sum: Bestwood winding engine is an industrial building. The building was built in 1873, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II* listed as Winding House and Headstocks at Bestwood Colliery.
